policy_title: Hold Water Companies Accountable and Invest Fines
stated: The Conservative Party will work with the regulator to further hold water companies to account, including banning executive bonuses for serious criminal breaches, and will invest fines from water companies into river restoration projects.

source.quote: Working with the regulator to further hold companies to account, including banning executive bonuses if a company has committed a serious criminal breach. This will build on our legislation for unlimited fines. ...Using fines from water companies to invest in river restoration projects...

bearing_set.reason: Investing fines into river restoration and holding water companies to account for criminal breaches directly targets water quality — a core O6 indicator.

membership_note: The two policy levers (executive bonus ban, fines-to-restoration) both operate through the same channel: reducing water-company pollution and repairing river ecosystems — squarely O6. The bonus ban references 'serious criminal breaches' but functions as a corporate-governance deterrent rather than a measure that moves O5 indicators (crime rates, court backlogs, justice system capacity); that link is too peripheral to clear the non-negligible bar. No other fundamental is materially affected: the revenue involved is fines redirected (not new fiscal flows material enough to bear on O12), and effects on O15 (community belonging via cleaner rivers) or O4 (executive pay) are incidental and do not clear the non-negligible threshold.
